record.file_problem: none; the full LessWrong post is present
record.tranche_reason: It measures SAE feature extraction from a text-only model and tests text-derived steering in multimodal models, providing indirect evidence relevant to V4. It does not reproduce the toy-model superposition experiment.
record.gate_note: The post reports SAE feature extraction and steering outcomes, plus other text-derived steering demonstrations relevant to cross-modal representations. It does not test feature competition, capacity pressure, polysemanticity, or whether SAE features are complete or canonical. The CV-Bench parameter search and layer-selection procedure are described, but no numerical CV-Bench outcomes are given.
record.test_reason: The post uses pretrained GemmaScope SAEs as one way to extract steering vectors. It reports only how well its steering methods improve visual reasoning in multimodal models. It does not measure whether features are superposed, spread across neurons, or recoverable by a dictionary. The '<10 features' figure counts features kept after o3-mini filtering, a selection step. It is not evidence of sparse features in the model.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that steering vectors derived from text improve MLLM visual reasoning and alter visual judgments, which suggests text and vision share representations. Mean shift works best and prompting barely helps. Limitations they note: the method needs a text backbone, depends on vector quality, and was tested only on early-fusion architectures (PaliGemma, Idefics3).
record.recipe_differences: The post does not apply or reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method; it extracts text-derived concept vectors and adds them to multimodal model activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with steering strength in the color demonstration. The post also tunes layer and strength on CV-Bench and selects token type using small validation subsets for the out-of-distribution evaluations.

fits_no_version.finding: Text-derived steering vectors (MeanShift +7.6%, SAE +6.0%, Probe +3.9% overall) improve out-of-distribution visual reasoning in PaliGemma2/Idefics3. A text 'red' vector shifts PaliGemma2-10B's color report as α increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept directions from a text backbone transfer to and steer visual processing in multimodal LLMs built on that backbone.

record.problems: The post does not give individual model results for most reported aggregate gains, uncertainty estimates, or detailed baseline values for several results. SAE feature relevance is described as filtered and checked with GPT-o3-mini, but no independent recovery or completeness evaluation is reported. The post says full technical details are in a linked paper, which is not included here.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for CV-Bench grid-search outcomes: the post describes the search and qualitative conclusions but gives no numerical CV-Bench results. The prompting result (+1.0%) is a comparison method rather than a result about the claim's feature or representation object.

untested.parts: Toy models, sparsity transition, geometry: none of these are studied.
Capacity competition and dedicated dimensions are not studied.
Non-capacity causes of polysemanticity are not studied.
SAEs are used as a tool. Feature distribution across neurons and the quality of SAE recovery are not measured.
Completeness, stability and canonical status of SAE features are not studied.
Dimensionality of features is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong summary of arXiv:2505.14071. SAEs appear only as an off-the-shelf extraction tool, so no version verdict is warranted. The reader's V4 'supports' label should be dropped. The CLEVR +34.2% headline is not recorded as its own row but is irrelevant to any version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse-feature capacity, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or gives important features dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

The post does not measure how features are distributed across neurons, compare SAE features with other dictionaries, or establish coverage and recovery quality beyond its stated feature filtering and steering results. The SAE extraction is from text-only model activations; multimodal-model feature extraction is not tested.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features.
Whether the represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multi-dimensional.
